Introducing psa > Source Map

Source Map

Status: landed. The source map design recorded on this page has been implemented and promoted into the psa master tree (2026-11-27): dual presentation of diagnostics and the persistent .psa-map.json artefact are working features, verified by the close-out suite (7/7) and a post-promotion re-verification (4/4 — compiler test suite 17/17, diagnostic goldens 10/10, an 82-file full-coverage sweep byte-identical, and bidirectional map lookups byte-identical with their goldens). What remains future work is the debugger that will consume the map, not the map itself.

Why it was needed: three measured gaps

Before the map existed, when a psa program failed, the position in the message was often not a position in anything the author wrote (all three behaviours measured on 2026-11-26):

  • psa’s own diagnostics had a line but no column. A frontend error named the .psa file and the line; the column was always null, and there was no source excerpt.
  • When the generated code was refused downstream, the reported position was in the generated files. A 7-line .psa program expands to 3,171 lines of generated SLA and 78,486 lines of generated SA; a host trap reports the expanded SA line. Without a map, that number is noise to the psa author, and psa’s own wrapper added nothing but the generated file’s name.
  • A runtime panic carried a code and no position at all. An out-of-bounds program’s entire output was PANIC: code=32 — no psa line, no SLA line.

What has landed

Dual presentation of every diagnostic. When compilation fails, the generated SLA’s error is preserved verbatim — its code, its message, and its position in the generated file, unaltered and unreplaced — and, alongside it, psa presents the corresponding psa information: the .psa file, line and column, with a source excerpt. Neither half replaces the other; where a mapping can only be given at reduced precision, the presentation says so (the lookup reports the previous segment as approximate) rather than pretending exactness.

A machine-readable map that ships with the build output. The mapping is written to a sidecar file, <stem>.psa-map.json (format v1), next to the generated SLA, and copied next to the executable on a successful build. It records the sources (with hashes, so a stale map is detected rather than silently applied to a changed file), the segments connecting generated positions to psa positions with their origin and precision, prebuilt bidirectional indexes — psa line to generated positions, and generated line back to psa — and an index of panic sites. The psa map-loc command queries the map in both directions. The intended consumer is a future debugger: a breakpoint set on a psa line is resolved through this file to the generated positions it must stop at. The debugger itself is later work; the map is the interface it will consume. One boundary stays honest: the host’s bare runtime output for a panic is still just its code — the map’s panic-site index is what lets that code be traced back to candidate psa positions after the fact.

Registered residual gaps. A few anchors are still coarser than the rest and are recorded as such, not hidden: lambda and generator function-header anchors, line-level (not column-level) mapping for a small number of diagnostic kinds, and one lexer column-accounting choice still to be settled. None of them blocks the dual presentation or the map artefact above.

Key Points of This Page

  • Source map: landed — dual presentation and the .psa-map.json artefact are working, verified features.
  • Diagnostics are dual: the SLA error verbatim, plus the psa file, line, column, and excerpt; reduced-precision mappings are labelled approximate.
  • The map is a persistent artefact (.psa-map.json v1, bidirectional indexes, panic-site index), queryable via psa map-loc and intended for later breakpoint debugging in psa source.
